case_name: Tracey Rene Merrell and Christopher L. Merrell v. Commissioner

taxpayer.notes: Husband and wife, pro se. Notice of deficiency dated May 7, 2018.

adjustments: included Social Security benefits of $22,790 (85% of $26,812)
10% additional tax under 72(t) on $17,410 IRA distribution
notice_of_deficiency.contested_by_taxpayer: Inclusion of Social Security benefits (seeking 86(e) lump-sum treatment) and 72(t) additional tax (wife disabled; hardship)
conceded: Petitioners: failed to report interest income of $43
Petitioners: not entitled to deduct $5,000 IRA contribution
Petitioners: not entitled to deduct legal fees related to a bankruptcy proceeding
Respondent: no unreported wage income of $1,109

findings_of_fact.fact: Mrs. Merrell received $26,812 Social Security benefits in 2015, including $9,772 otherwise payable in 2014
findings_of_fact.snippet: Mrs. Merrell received Social Security benefits totaling $26,812, including benefits of $9,772 that were otherwise payable to her in 2014

findings_of_fact.fact: Mr. Merrell received $17,410 IRA distribution; under 59 1/2 and not disabled
findings_of_fact.snippet: Mr. Merrell received a distribution of $17,410 from an IRA. Mr. Merrell had not attained the age of 59½, nor was he disabled

findings_of_fact.fact: Joint 2015 return reported total income $67,658 = wages $50,248 + IRA distribution $17,410; no SS benefits reported; no 86(e) election
findings_of_fact.snippet: reporting total income of $67,658, comprising wages of $50,248 and the aforementioned IRA distribution of $17,410
Social Security benefits of $22,790 (representing 85% of the Social Security benefits of $26,812 paid to Mrs. Merrell)

findings_of_fact.fact: Post-NOD handwritten "1040X 2015" proposed $14,484 taxable SS; not processed
findings_of_fact.snippet: including the addition of "$14,484 for taxable social security income." The IRS did not process

findings_of_fact.fact: Amended 2014 return reported taxable SS $8,306 (85% of $9,772) and tax $1,284; not processed
findings_of_fact.snippet: reporting taxable Social Security benefits of $8,306 (representing 85% of the Social Security benefits of $9,772

findings_of_fact.fact: Parties agree Mr. Merrell (IRA owner) not disabled; petitioners argue Mrs. Merrell was disabled
findings_of_fact.snippet: the parties agree that he was not disabled during the year in issue

issues.question: Must petitioners include $22,790 of Social Security benefits in 2015 income, and would a §86(e) lump-sum election reduce their liability?
issues.holding: Respondent sustained; no 86(e) election on original return and petitioners offered no 2014 return or worksheets showing an election would alter liability
issues.computable_reason: Decided on failure of proof (no 2014 return/worksheets) regarding 86(e) effect; 85% inclusion itself is mechanical but needed inputs (2014 income) not in record

issues.question: Are petitioners liable for the 10% §72(t) additional tax on Mr. Merrell's $17,410 IRA distribution where Mrs. Merrell (not the IRA owner) was disabled?
issues.holding: Liable; disability exception requires the IRA owner (employee) to be disabled; no hardship exception
issues.computable_reason: Owner under 59 1/2 and not disabled; spouse disability irrelevant under 72(t)(5); 10% of $17,410

decision.text: Decision will be entered under Rule 155.
decision.summary: SS inclusion and 72(t) additional tax sustained; respondent conceded penalty and $1,109 wages; petitioners conceded interest, IRA deduction, legal fees

notes: Some facts stipulated. Footnote 4: petitioners acknowledge $26,812 received. Note the opinion says the $9,772 was paid in 2015 (p. 4) though otherwise payable in 2014. Derived: 85% x 26,812 = 22,790.2; 10% x 17,410 = 1,741 (not stated by court).
